trace.msg: Let's look at this puzzle carefully. I'll only move when I can explain why.

Going to number 2 leaves no safe move afterwards; going up-right would force the two-exit cells to link up into a loop (or put the numbers out of order) (and 1 more option fails too). So the line goes left.
Number 2 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Going up-right leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes right.
The line must go up-left: up-right is number 17, which comes later.
Going up-right would force the line onto number 17 before its turn. So the line goes left.
Going up-left would force the line onto number 6 before its turn. So the line goes up-right.
Going right would force the line onto number 17 before its turn; going up-left, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves (and 1 more option fails too). So the line goes left.
Going up-left would force the line onto number 7 before its turn; going up-right would strand number 6: it would be left with only one free neighbour. So the line goes down-left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes up-left.
Going up-left would force the line onto number 9 before its turn; going up-right, the next 3 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (2,-1). So the line goes right.
Going up-left leaves no safe move afterwards; going right, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes up-right.
Going right would leave number 9 unreachable without crossing a higher number; going down-right would leave number 9 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes left.
The line must go left: up-left is number 11, which comes later; up-right is number 13, which comes later.
Going up-left would turn number 9 into a dead-end pocket with no way out. So the line goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes up-right.
Going right would turn number 16 into a dead-end pocket with no way out; going down-right would strand number 16: it would be left with only one free neighbour. So the line goes up-right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down-right.
Going right would turn number 17 into a dead-end pocket with no way out. So the line goes down-right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes up-right.
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
